title: 2002 HMMT February Geometry Problem 3
statement: A square and a regular hexagon are drawn with the same side length. If the area of the square is \(\sqrt{3}\), what is the area of the hexagon?

solutions.text: The hexagon is composed of six equilateral triangles each of side length \(\sqrt[4]{3}\) (with base \(b=\sqrt[4]{3}\) and height \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} b\) ), so the total area is \(\frac{9}{2}\).
